title: Timezone picker is inert: all 18 options are IANA names, and the clock parser accepts none of them — every displayed time silently stays on the host's timezone
what_happened: Settings > Location > Time: I turned 'Use system time' OFF and set Timezone = America/Los_Angeles, then Asia/Tokyo, then UTC. app_settings.timezone and use_system_time persist correctly each time, but NOTHING on screen changes: the status-bar clock stayed 14:44 (host America/New_York) when it should have read 11:44 PDT / 03:44 JST / 18:44 UTC, the Dashboard header clock stayed host-local, and the Dashboard twilight strip stayed byte-identical (Sunset 23:48 / Astro dark 02:00 / Astro dawn 06:31 / Sunrise 08:43) across all three timezones. Root cause in source: packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/providers/clock_provider.dart:219 _parseTimezoneOffset accepts only 'UTC' or 'UTC+HH[:MM]' and returns null for anything else, so clockProvider falls back to SystemClock for all 17 IANA entries the picker offers. The fallback is completely silent — the file's own comment claims 'Failure to parse is explicit and logged at the Clock.fromUtc call sites', but nothing appears in app.log (grep for timezone/clock/tz over the whole 151-line log: zero hits).
expected: Picking a site timezone must change displayed times, or the picker must not exist. clockProvider feeds imaging_service capture timestamps, session_provider and scheduler_provider, so a remote-observatory operator who sets the site timezone gets host-local timestamps on their frames and host-local scheduler decisions while the UI shows the timezone they chose.
repro: Settings > Location, scroll to Time. Toggle 'Use system time' OFF. Set Timezone = Asia/Tokyo. Look at the status-bar clock and at Dashboard > twilight strip. Repeat with America/Los_Angeles and UTC.
evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rsg/24-status.png (LA, sys-time on: 14:43), /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rsg/25-status.png (LA, sys-time OFF: 14:44 — unchanged), /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rsg/27-status.png (Asia/Tokyo, sys-time OFF: 14:44), /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rsg/31-status.png (UTC, sys-time OFF: 14:46 while `date -u` says 18:46), /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rsg/28-crop.png (twilight strip unchanged under Asia/Tokyo). sqlite3 confirms timezone/use_system_time persisted each time.

title: 'Use Device Location' is IP geolocation labelled as GPS, and it leaves the old elevation in place — producing a site that does not exist
what_happened: The row reads 'Use Device Location / Get location from GPS'. Clicking it on Linux desktop returned 'Location updated: Newtown Square, Pennsylvania, United States' and wrote observer_latitude=39.9817, observer_longitude=-75.4072 — but observer_elevation stayed at 1234.0, the value from the previous (Seattle) site. The stored site is now a Pennsylvania coordinate at 1234 m; the highest point in Pennsylvania is 979 m. The success message says 'Location updated' with no hint that one of the three fields was not updated. Source: location_settings.dart:270 passes `elevation: settings.elevation` unchanged, and GeolocationService.fetchLocationFromGPS() (packages/skotiq_planetarium/lib/src/services/geolocation_service.dart:7-14) is not GPS at all — it does an HTTPS GET to the third-party service https://ipapi.co/json/.
expected: (a) Do not call it GPS when it is IP geolocation — say 'Estimate from IP address (city-level, ~10 km)'. (b) Either fetch/clear elevation, or say plainly that elevation was not changed and needs review. (c) Disclose that clicking sends the user's IP to a third party before doing it — this is a silent outbound request from an app people run on isolated observatory networks.
repro: Settings > Location > set elevation to 1234 and latitude 47.6062 (Seattle). Click the crosshair on 'Use Device Location'. Read the snackbar, then sqlite3 app_settings observer_*.
evidence: Snackbar text captured via tree: 'Location updated: Newtown Square, Pennsylvania, United States'. sqlite3 immediately after: observer_latitude|39.9817, observer_longitude|-75.4072, observer_elevation|1234.0.

title: Files & Storage says 'Last backup: Never' while Settings > Advanced > Backup & Restore says 'Last Full Backup: Aug 2, 2026 10:30' — same app, same second, same fact
what_happened: The scratch instance ran its startup backup check at 10:27:45 local: three .nsbackup files were written and app_settings got autosave.last_backup_at = 2026-08-02T14:27:45.635595Z. I then opened Settings > Files & Storage at 10:28 and scrolled to Status. At 10:30:02 the card still read 'Last backup / Never' with the trailing status 'Pending'. Clicking 'Back Up Now' immediately corrected it to 'Last backup / 0s ago' and 'In 23h', so the widget can render a real value — it just never picks up the backup the app itself performed. STRONGER REPRO: I then restarted the app (same profile, same DB). With autosave.last_backup_at = 2026-08-02T14:30:25.957100Z persisted and four .nsbackup files on disk, a freshly opened Settings > Files & Storage again reads 'Last backup / Never' and 'Pending'. So the persisted timestamp is never hydrated into the card at all; the only thing that makes it truthful is pressing Back Up Now in the current session, and that truth is lost on the next launch. DIRECT CONTRADICTION BETWEEN TWO SURFACES: in the same session and within seconds of each other, Settings > ADVANCED > Backup & Restore > Auto-Save Status reads 'Last Full Backup: Aug 2, 2026 10:30' and lists the real files under Recent Backups, while Settings > GENERAL > Files & Storage > Status reads 'Last backup / Never' and 'Pending'. Backup & Restore hydrates from the persisted key correctly; Files & Storage does not.
expected: The Status card must reflect the persisted autosave.last_backup_at (and any backup completed in this session). 'Never' is a false statement about the user's data-protection state: the natural reaction is to assume backups are broken, or to conclude they are working when they are not.
repro: Press 'Back Up Now' (card correctly shows '7m ago' / 'In 23h'), then stop and relaunch the app with the same profile and reopen Settings > Files & Storage: the card is back to 'Never' / 'Pending' while sqlite3 app_settings still holds autosave.last_backup_at and the .nsbackup files are still on disk.
evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rsg2/07-files-scroll.png ('Last backup / Never', trailing 'Pending') taken at 10:30:02; sqlite3 app_settings autosave.last_backup_at = 2026-08-02T14:27:45.635595Z; ls ~/Documents/Skotiq/backups shows skotiq_autosave_2026-08-02T10-27-45.572326.nsbackup. After clicking Back Up Now the tree reads 'Status / 0s ago' + 'In 23h' and the key becomes 14:30:25.957100Z. After restart (pid 2190911): tree shows 'panel: Status / panel: Never / panel: Last backup / panel: Pending' while sqlite3 gives autosave.last_backup_at|2026-08-02T14:30:25.957100Z and ~/Documents/Skotiq/backups holds 4 files from this run. Same-session comparison: tree of ADVANCED > Backup & Restore = 'Auto-Save Status / Last Sequence Save Never / Last Full Backup Aug 2, 2026 10:30' plus a Recent Backups list containing skotiq_autosave_2026-08-02T10-30-25.892145.nsbackup; tree of GENERAL > Files & Storage taken immediately after = 'panel: Status / panel: Never / panel: Last backup / panel: Pending'. /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rsg2/46-backup-restore.png.

title: INDI 'Test Connection' reports a green 'Connected. Found 0 devices.' for an address nothing can connect to
what_happened: Settings > Connection > INDI Server Address > Configure. I set the host to 192.0.2.1 (RFC 5737 TEST-NET-1, guaranteed unroutable) port 7624 and pressed Test Connection: after ~6 s the dialog showed a green check and 'Connected. Found 0 devices.' I repeated with 127.0.0.1 port 9 (discard port, connection refused instantly): same green 'Connected. Found 0 devices.' A raw TCP probe of 192.0.2.1:7624 from the same machine hangs until killed, and nothing listens on 127.0.0.1:9. Nothing was written to app.log for either attempt (grep for 'address discovery failed' / '192.0.2' -> no hits).
expected: Test Connection must distinguish 'reached an INDI server that reports no drivers' from 'could not reach anything'. On failure it should say so, and name the failure (timed out / connection refused / not an INDI server). The whole point of the button is to tell the operator, before dark, whether the address is right.
repro: Settings > Connection > INDI Server Address > Configure > set host 192.0.2.1, port 7624 > Test Connection. Then host 127.0.0.1, port 9 > Test Connection.
evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rsg2/24-indi-test.png (192.0.2.1:7624 -> green 'Connected. Found 0 devices.') and /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rsg2/26-dlg3.png (127.0.0.1:9 -> same). `timeout 8 bash -c 'echo > /dev/tcp/192.0.2.1/7624'` exits 124 (hung). Root cause: packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/backend/ffi_backend/discovery_camera_operations.dart:86-102 `_discoverAddressDevices` catches every exception and returns `const <DeviceInfo>[]`, so the dialog's catch block at indi_server_dialog.dart:131 can never fire and line 129 always renders the success string. || RE-CONFIRMED 2026-08-02 on display :81 (profile r-settings-general) with two fresh cases: (a) 127.0.0.1:7624 with nothing listening (verified by 'ss -ltn' showing no listener on 7624) returned a green check and 'Connected. Found 0 devices.'; (b) host 'no-such-host.invalid' port 7624 - a name that cannot resolve in DNS - returned the same green 'Connected. Found 0 devices.' Screenshot: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rsg3/47-dialog-crop.png. Port validation in the same dialog DOES work (999999 -> 'Port must be between 1 and 65535.' and Save blocked), so the dialog validates syntax but never validates reachability.

title: Auto-Save & Backups renders compiled-in defaults instead of the saved settings, and changing any one field silently overwrites the other four
what_happened: Before restarting, I set 'Enable sequence auto-save' ON (autosave.sequence_enabled=true) and 'Maximum backups' to 50 (autosave.max_backups=50), both confirmed in sqlite3. After an app restart with the same profile, Settings > Files & Storage > Auto-Save & Backups renders the DEFAULTS: 'Enable sequence auto-save' OFF, 'Maximum backups' 7, 'Last backup' Never — while the database still held sequence_enabled=true, max_backups=50, last_backup_at=2026-08-02T14:30:25Z. I then changed only 'Backup interval' from 24 to 12. sqlite3 immediately after: backup_interval_hours=12 (correct), but autosave.sequence_enabled had flipped true->false and autosave.max_backups 50->7. One edit to an unrelated field destroyed two saved settings, including turning a data-protection feature OFF, with no warning.
expected: The page must render the persisted config, and an edit must be a partial update, not a full rewrite from stale in-memory state. As shipped, a user who configures this page loses it on the next launch and gets it silently reverted the moment they touch anything.
repro: Settings > Files & Storage: turn 'Enable sequence auto-save' ON, set 'Maximum backups' 50. Confirm with sqlite3. Stop and relaunch the app. Reopen the page: switch shows OFF, Maximum backups shows 7. Change 'Backup interval' to 12. sqlite3: sequence_enabled=false, max_backups=7.
evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rsg2/39-autosave900.png (post-restart page: auto-save OFF, Maximum backups 7, Last backup Never) against sqlite3 output at the same moment: autosave.sequence_enabled|true, autosave.max_backups|50, autosave.last_backup_at|2026-08-02T14:30:25.957100Z. After editing Backup interval: autosave.sequence_enabled|false, autosave.backup_interval_hours|12, autosave.max_backups|7.
where: packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/settings/widgets/auto_save_settings.dart:178-180 watches `autoSaveServiceProvider` (the raw service) rather than `autoSaveLifecycleProvider`, which is the provider that loads the persisted config (packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/services/auto_save_service.dart:783-810). _updateConfig at auto_save_settings.dart:68-84 does `service.config.copyWith(...)` and `_persistAutoSaveConfig` (auto_save_service.dart:854-861) writes all five autosave.* keys, so the stale defaults are written back over the saved values.

title: One failed 'Connect to Server' attempt drops the app out of Local mode permanently — every screen gets an undismissable red 'Error: not connected to server' banner and there is no way back without a restart
what_happened: The app was running standalone: Settings > Connection reported 'Connection Status / Local' with a 'Local Mode' badge. I opened Connect to Server, left the prefilled localhost:8080 (nothing listening) and pressed Connect. It correctly reported 'Connection failed: Connection to http://localhost:8080 did not complete (state=disconnected)'. But after dismissing the dialog the app did NOT return to Local: Settings > Connection now reads 'Server Status / Not connected' and 'Connection Status / Disconnected', and a full-width red banner 'Error: not connected to server' is pinned under the title bar on EVERY screen (verified on Dashboard, Settings and Equipment). The banner has no close button, and the title-bar connection popover just says 'Connection Status / Not connected to a server' with no action. Nothing on the Connection page offers 'use local' or 'disconnect' — the only control is 'Connect' again.
expected: A failed attempt to reach an OPTIONAL remote host must leave the local backend intact, or must offer an obvious 'Continue locally'. Standing up a scary red error bar on a machine that is working perfectly well locally is the cry-wolf pattern: the next time that bar means something, nobody will read it.
repro: Fresh desktop profile, no pairing. Settings > Connection > Connect to Server > Connect (defaults localhost:8080). Dismiss the dialog. Look at the banner on any screen, and reopen Settings > Connection.
evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rsg2/30-banner.png and /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rsg2/31-dash-banner.png (banner on Dashboard); /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rsg2/36-connstatus.png (title-bar popover, no action); tree of Settings > Connection after the attempt: 'panel: Server Status / panel: Not connected / panel: Connection Status / panel: Disconnected' where it previously read 'Local' / 'Local Mode'. Banner condition is packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/shell/app_shell.dart:659-670 `ref.watch(sequencerBackendProvider) is DisconnectedBackend`.
where: packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/shell/app_shell.dart:653-671; connection/backend swap in packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/settings/widgets/connection_settings.dart (Connect to Server dialog)

title: Selecting Spanish translates only the nav rail and Settings; every other screen stays English
what_happened: Settings > General > Language > Spanish. The nav rail and the whole Settings tree translate correctly (Ajustes/Apariencia/Ubicacion/Archivos y almacenamiento) and app_settings.language flips to 'es'. But the Dashboard renders 100% English: 'TONIGHT'S BRIEFING', 'No run active', 'Image tonight', 'Plan Tonight', 'Set an observing location for twilight times.', "Tonight's targets", 'Readiness', 'Edit Dashboard'. The persistent bottom status bar is also English on every screen ('Camera Disconnected', 'Mount Disconnected', 'Guider Disconnected', 'Focus', 'No save path', 'Dashboard'). The Spanish subtitle under the setting reads 'Elegir el idioma de la interfaz principal' (choose the language of the MAIN interface), which is not what it does.
expected: Either translate the product surfaces too, or label the control honestly and scope it (the English subtitle 'app chrome' is closer to the truth than the Spanish one). Shipping a language picker that leaves the main working screens untranslated is worse than not offering the language.
repro: Fresh profile -> Settings > General -> Language dropdown -> Spanish -> click Dashboard in nav rail -> tree shows all English strings.
evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rsg/05-spanish.png (Settings fully Spanish, status bar English); tree of Dashboard after switching: 0 of ~12 visible dashboard strings translated. sqlite3 app_settings language='es'.
where: packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/settings/widgets/general_settings.dart:79-93 (SettingsDropdown offers languageEnglish/languageSpanish); localization coverage in packages/skotiq_app/lib/localization/

title: Red night mode leaves the Moon phase disc near-white — a dark-adaptation flare on the default screen
what_happened: With Theme = Red night, the Dashboard's Moon card renders a ~50 px filled disc at RGB(214,220,226) (luminance 219) on a background of RGB(10,0,0). It is by far the brightest object on screen and it is bluish-white, exactly the wavelength red-night mode exists to suppress. Everything else on the dashboard is correctly red-shifted.
expected: Red night should red-shift or dim the moon graphic like everything else (e.g. desaturate to a red-grey ramp). A user at the eyepiece opens the dashboard and gets a white disc in the face.
repro: Settings > Appearance > Theme > Red night, then click Dashboard in the nav rail. Moon card, left column.

title: At UI scale Extra Large (1.4x) the bottom status bar overlaps itself — the run-state chip is painted under the temperature group

title: 'Sync from Server' reports 'Location synced from server' on a standalone desktop session where there is no server
what_happened: With the app running standalone (no headless host paired, backend = local), clicking the download-cloud on 'Sync from Server / Fetch location from Headless Server' shows a green success snackbar 'Location synced from server'. Nothing was fetched from any server: the handler calls profileSettingsBackendProvider.getLocation(), which on a local session returns the location this same app just wrote, so the values were unchanged (47.6062 / -122.3321 / 1234 before and after).
expected: The row should be hidden or disabled when no headless host is connected — exactly the way the same file already hides 'Start minimized' and 'Confirm before closing' in remote mode. A green 'synced from server' when there is no server is a false claim, and it trains the user to trust that message when it matters.
repro: Fresh desktop profile, no pairing. Settings > Location > click the icon on the 'Sync from Server' row.
evidence: tree captured the snackbar 'Location synced from server'; sqlite3 app_settings observer_* identical before and after the click.

title: Importing a detailed .hor horizon silently collapses it to 8 sector maxima — a single tree blocks a whole 45-degree sector
what_happened: I imported a 36-point .hor file (one sample every 10 deg of azimuth, altitudes 10-29 deg). The snackbar said 'Horizon profile imported from test36.hor' and the eight compass fields filled in as N=25, NE=16, E=21, SE=25, S=29, SW=14, W=19, NW=23. Those are exactly the MAXIMUM sample in each 45 deg sector — the other 28 samples were discarded with no mention. Source confirms this is deliberate (location_settings.dart:498-501, 'highest altitude per sector wins'), but nothing in the UI says so.
expected: Real horizon files from Stellarium/HorizonBox have 1-degree resolution and are the reason people generate them. Max-per-sector means one 29-degree tree at azimuth 190 marks everything from 157.5 to 202.5 as blocked, so the planner and Tonight will refuse targets that are actually clear — this costs imaging time on exactly the targets a southern-horizon site cares about. At minimum the import must say 'imported 36 samples, reduced to 8 sectors (worst case per sector)'. Better: store the full profile and interpolate.
repro: Create a .hor with one line per 10 deg azimuth; Settings > Location > Local Horizon Mask > Import .hor / CSV; compare the eight resulting fields with the file.
evidence: Input /tmp/ns-audit/rsg-files/test36.hor; resulting horizon_profile_json from sqlite3: {"N":25.0,"NE":16.0,"E":21.0,"SE":25.0,"S":29.0,"SW":14.0,"W":19.0,"NW":23.0} — verified by hand to be the per-sector maxima. Snackbar text captured from tree.

title: Settings search sends autofocus queries to Files & Storage — the generated index for that page contains the whole Autofocus page's strings
what_happened: Typing 'Backlash' in the Settings search box returns two sections and ranks 'Files & Storage' FIRST, above 'Autofocus'. Files & Storage contains no backlash setting at all (its only rows are Image output, Sequences, Database and logs, sequence auto-save, and backups). Same for 'V-curve' and 'Disable guiding during AF' — both list Files & Storage first. Root cause: the generated index packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/settings/settings_search_index.g.dart:247 gives 'files-storage' 75 keywords, of which ~40 belong to Autofocus / Predictive Autofocus ('Backlash IN', 'Backlash OUT', 'Curve fitting strategy', 'Designated autofocus filter', 'Steps out from center for V-curve', 'Use brightest n stars', 'Stop autoguider while focusing', 'Inner/Outer crop ratio', 'High-confidence threshold (R²)', ...).
expected: A search for a setting's visible name must land on the page that actually contains it. As shipped, the search box's top hit for an autofocus term is a page where that setting does not exist — the user clicks it, finds nothing, and concludes the setting is gone.
repro: Settings > search box > type 'Backlash'. Results: Files & Storage (highlighted/first), Autofocus. Click Files & Storage — no backlash control anywhere on the page.
evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rsg2/search-montage3.png (Backlash / Image output / V-curve / Disable guiding during AF all list Files & Storage first). Index dump of 'files-storage' shows the Autofocus strings.

title: Settings search is a raw substring match, so any two-word phrase a user would actually type ('capture folder') returns 'No settings match your search'
what_happened: Search 'capture folder' -> 'No settings match your search.' Search 'folder' alone -> Files & Storage, Autofocus, Image Grading. Search 'disk' -> no match, although the Dashboard's own empty-state text is 'Set a capture directory to track free space' and the status bar says 'No save path'. The matcher only finds a result when the typed string is a literal substring of one indexed phrase, so it cannot AND two words together.
expected: Tokenise the query and AND the terms (NINA, macOS System Settings and Windows Settings all do this). The words the app itself uses elsewhere for this feature — 'capture', 'disk', 'free space', 'save path' — should all reach Files & Storage.
repro: Settings > search box > 'capture folder' (no match); then 'folder' (3 matches); then 'disk' (no match).
evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rsg2/search-montage.png panel 4 ('capture folder' -> No settings match your search.), /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rsg2/search-montage2.png ('folder' -> 3 hits, 'disk' -> none).

title: Automatic backups are ON by default and write to ~/Documents/Skotiq/backups, a location the Files & Storage page never names and offers no way to change
what_happened: 'Enable automatic backups' defaults ON with a 24 h interval and 'Maximum backups 7'. The page shows File Paths for 'Image output' and 'Sequences' and says application data is 'Managed automatically in Skotiq's application data folder' — but it never says where backups go. They go to getApplicationDocumentsDirectory()/Skotiq/backups, i.e. ~/Documents/Skotiq/backups, which ignores SKOTIQ_DATA_DIR entirely: this sandboxed audit instance, whose data dir is /tmp/ns-audit/r-settings-general/data, wrote its backups into the real user's Documents folder. 'Maximum backups' then PRUNES files in that undisclosed directory.
expected: The Status section should show the backup folder path with a 'Reveal' action and let the user change it (backups belong on the same drive the user actually backs up, and an observatory PC's Documents folder is often the smallest volume). Retention that deletes files must name the folder it deletes from. Honouring the configured data directory is the minimum.
repro: Fresh profile with SKOTIQ_DATA_DIR=/tmp/ns-audit/r-settings-general/data. Wait 5 min or press Back Up Now. `find /tmp/ns-audit/r-settings-general -iname '*backup*'` -> nothing; `ls ~/Documents/Skotiq/backups` -> skotiq_autosave_2026-08-02T10-27-45.572326.nsbackup and two more from this run.
evidence: backup_service.dart:1025-1030 `_getBackupDirectory` = getApplicationDocumentsDirectory()/Skotiq/backups with no settings override wired up; observed files listed above; /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rsg2/07-files-scroll.png shows the Status card with no path.

title: The Alpaca server address can never be set: 'Query Alpaca on startup' points at a 'configured Alpaca server' that no screen in the app configures
what_happened: Settings > Connection > Discovery has 'INDI Server Address — localhost:7624' with a Configure button, and directly under it 'Query Alpaca on startup / Include the configured Alpaca server in automatic startup discovery'. There is no Alpaca Server Address row anywhere on the page (I scrolled the whole page). app_settings does hold alpaca_server_host=localhost and alpaca_server_port=11111, and skotiq_core exposes setAlpacaServerHost/setAlpacaServerPort — but `grep -rl alpacaServerHost packages/skotiq_app/lib` returns nothing, so no UI ever calls them. The Alpaca discovery address is therefore permanently localhost:11111.
expected: Alpaca is the cross-platform path this very page recommends ('Cross-platform ASCOM devices should use Alpaca'), and the common deployment is an ASCOM Remote / Alpaca device on ANOTHER machine on the LAN. An Alpaca Server Address row with the same Configure + Test affordance as INDI is required, or the toggle's subtitle must stop claiming there is a configured server.
repro: Settings > Connection, scroll the full page. Only INDI has an address row. Toggle 'Query Alpaca on startup' on; there is no way to say where.
evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rsg2/20-connection.png and /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rsg2/21-conn-bottom.png (the entire page, top and bottom). sqlite3 app_settings: alpaca_server_host|localhost, alpaca_server_port|11111. connection_settings.dart mentions Alpaca only at lines 177-182 (the toggle).

title: The session checkpoint lives outside the database, so the app offers to resume a sequence its own database has never heard of — and the failure dialog contradicts itself
what_happened: On launch, a profile whose database contains ZERO rows in sequences, sequence_nodes, sequence_runs, sequence_checkpoints, sequence_versions and captured_images was shown 'Recover Sequence? / A previous sequence was interrupted and can be resumed. / Sequence: New Sequence / Saved: 0m ago / Completed: 4 frames (0m integration)'. The claim of 4 completed frames is untrue for the database this instance is using. Pressing Resume produced, inside the SAME dialog: 'Recovery did not complete — Exception: No valid checkpoint to resume from' immediately followed by 'The checkpoint is still available. Retry resume or discard it to start fresh.' — two contradictory statements, one of them a raw Dart exception string, while the header still asserts '4 frames' were completed.
expected: The recovery prompt must be scoped to the database in use (store the checkpoint in the DB, or key the file to the database identity), the frame count must come from that database, and a failed resume must not simultaneously say the checkpoint is invalid and still available.
repro: Launch with SKOTIQ_DATABASE_DIR pointed at an empty scratch database while a checkpoint file exists at ~/.local/share/com.skotiq.desktop/skotiq_session.checkpoint. The dialog appears; press Resume.

title: The settings search index indexes confirmation-dialog titles the user can never see, while missing headings that are on screen
what_happened: Typing 'GLADE' into the settings search returns nothing, even though Settings > Catalogs renders a card headed 'GLADE+ Galaxy Catalog'. Meanwhile 'Delete Deep-Star Tiles' - the title of a destructive confirmation dialog, never rendered as a settings row - matches and returns Catalogs, and 'Roll back this rig' (another dialog title) returns Appliance Updates. The generated index bears this out: catalogs -> ['Delete Annotation Catalog','Delete Catalogs','Delete Deep-Star Tiles','HYG Star Database','OpenNGC'], updates -> ['Appliance Updates','Roll back this rig?'], equipment-profiles -> ['Could not load profiles','Select a profile'] (its own visible rows are absent, and so is the string 'Equipment Profiles').
expected: settings_search_index.g.dart's header states the source of truth is 'the title: of every row each settings section actually renders, so typing a setting's visible name finds it'. Visible headings like 'GLADE+ Galaxy Catalog' must be findable; dialog titles and error strings ('Could not load profiles') must not be, because matching them makes the search look like it works while it is matching text the user has never seen.
repro: Settings > search 'GLADE' -> 'No settings match your search'. Settings > Catalogs shows the GLADE+ Galaxy Catalog card. Now search 'Delete Deep-Star Tiles' -> Catalogs, and 'Roll back this rig' -> Appliance Updates.

title: The whole Settings section navigator is mouse-only: no tab stop, no focus ring, and every entry is exposed as a panel rather than a button
what_happened: I clicked the Settings search box and pressed Tab 24 times, grabbing the sidebar region (230x580 at root 245,312) after every press and diffing it against the baseline: all 24 captures were pixel-identical (0 changed pixels, diff bbox None). Focus never lands on any of the 7 group headers or 35 section entries. Tab from the search box instead jumps to the window title bar - one Tab then Enter opened the 'Transient Alerts' popover in the top-right - and further Tabs go into the detail pane (three Tabs then Enter opened the UI scale dropdown). The accessibility tree agrees: every sidebar entry appears as 'panel: General', 'panel: Appearance', 'panel: Connection', while genuine buttons on the same screen appear as 'button: Test Connection', 'button: Save'. Source confirms it: _GroupHeader and _CategoryItem in settings_screen.dart are a bare GestureDetector inside a MouseRegion, with no Focus, no InkWell and no Semantics(button: true).
expected: Every settings section should be a real focusable control: reachable by Tab/Shift-Tab, activatable with Enter/Space, drawing a visible focus indicator, and reported to AT as a button (or a selectable list item) with its selected state. Today a keyboard-only or screen-reader user cannot change settings sections at all.
repro: Settings > click the search box > press Tab repeatedly. The sidebar never shows focus; the first Tab+Enter opens the title-bar Transient Alerts popover. Compare 'drive_linux.py tree': sidebar rows are 'panel:', real buttons are 'button:'.
evidence: Live drive on display :81, profile r-settings-general. 25 region captures /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rsg3/kb-base.png and kb-1..kb-24.png, all identical by PIL ImageChops (changed_px 0, bbox None) for every one of the 24 tab stops. Title-bar activation captured at /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rsg3/56-kbd.png. Source: packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/settings/settings_screen.dart lines ~479 (_GroupHeader) and ~881 (_CategoryItem). Contrast that proves the app CAN do this: the main navigation rail uses NavItem (packages/skotiq_ui/lib/src/components/nav_item.dart), which is an InkWell - it takes focus and paints a highlight - so the rail is keyboard reachable while the settings section list beside it is not.
